ghat-p01-v01.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v01.question: Is desire and absence one event or two?
premises: Kāma arises in the heart, to kill.
This, the separated beloved, arises.
ghat-p01-v01.inference: Desire and absence arise as one event.

ghat-p01-v02.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v02.question: Who is the rival?
premises: By the cruel foreign-land-server, you will kill me without him.
ghat-p01-v02.inference: Foreign land the rival; service abroad the betrayal.

ghat-p01-v03.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v03.question: Release which love?
premises: Release foreign-land love today, or your wife — what is to be said?

ghat-p01-v04.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v04.question: What does the cātaka figure?
premises: The cātaka, thirsty, begs water.
The suffering traveler, she is your beloved.
ghat-p01-v04.inference: Cātaka figures lover thirsting for absent beloved.
uncertainties: Literal rain-bird vs figurative lover (both live).

ghat-p01-v05.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v05.question: What answers mood?
premises: By clouds the peacock-flock is sounded.
What delight, beloved, without me today?

ghat-p01-v06.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v06.question: Who thinned, who tormented?
premises: Thinned by cloud-arrival, tormented by hard Kāma.

ghat-p01-v07.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v07.question: What protects the fallen?
premises: Fallen into sorrow-ocean's water.
Remembrance of your virtue alone protects her.

ghat-p01-v08.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v08.question: Why unregarded?
premises: Rivers' water melts impurity.
Why regard me not, wretched?

ghat-p01-v09.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p01-v09.question: When ends burning?
premises: Pained by deep cloud-thunder.
When abandon, friend, separation-born sorrow-burning?

ghat-p02-v10.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p02-v10.question: For whose sake shine groves?
premises: For Kāma's sake, groves of abodes shine today.

ghat-p02-v11.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p02-v11.question: Who chief of groves?
premises: You are chief of groves by sprouts, eye-festival of youths.

ghat-p02-v12.speaker: Abhinavagupta (commentator-poet voice)
ghat-p02-v12.question: Mocked or loved?
premises: Kuṭaja, why laughed at by flowers?
I bow, hard to laugh at you.

essence: Śṛṅgāra is performed, not described: the separated beloved's voice, her appeal to the cloud, and the landscape's answering her are all determinants (vibhāva) of the rasa. The cloud is never told to carry a message — that is dhvani, and it is what makes it the genre's first instance. The voice closes not in despair but in sustaining memory: the sthāyibhāva (love) transforms the sorrow (vyabhicāri) into something relishable. Kāma arises in the heart to kill; the beloved who is absent arises with him; the cātaka, thirsty for rain alone, begs water; the peacock-flock sounds at the clouds; she is protected only by remembrance of his virtue.

rasa.sthayibhava: rati (love) transformed by viyoga (separation) into karuṇa-adjacent longing
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is love (rati), made relishable by separation (viyoga) as vibhāva; sorrow (śoka) is vyabhicāri, integrated not dissolved. The cloud is never told to carry a message — dhvani. Application, not attribution.

essence: Beauty is not decoration but cause: the groves shine for Kāma's sake, not the reverse. The grove is the vibhāva (determinant) of śṛṅgāra; the rasa overwhelms perception — dust of passion obscures sun and moon, new-cloud-drunk peacocks cry. The kuṭaja's mockery and the nīpa's release are consequents (anubhāva), not ornament: the poet sides with the humble tree over showy flowers. The bee kisses the yūthikā creeper. The rasa is aesthetic: the rasa IS the point.

rasa.sthayibhava: rati (love) in the grove; the beloved IS the sprout (mañjarī)
rasa.justification: The grove is vibhāva, not backdrop: 'for Kāma's sake the groves shine.' The sthāyibhāva transforms the landscape (rajas obscuring sun/moon) into its own body. Kuṭaja mockery and nīpa release are anubhāva. The rasa overwhelms perception.

essence: The rasa shifts from śṛṅgāra to vira/adbhuta: love and landscape are framed by the poet's skill, not by love alone. Clouds thundering make travelers long; sorrow grows, endless. Lovers honor the love-festival; cloud-arrival, dear friend, they bring. Then the tribute: may I be conquered by which poet, by yamakas; to him I pour water in ghaṭakarpara. The sthāyibhāva (love) resolves into the poet's own delight (camatkāra) at his craft. The potsherd is both vessel and namesake — the potsherd names itself at its close.

rasa.dominant: vira/adbhuta (heroic skill + wonder at craft), resolving from śṛṅgāra
rasa.sthayibhava: rati (love) resolving into camatkāra (wonder at the yamaka)
rasa.justification: The rasa shifts: the lover's voice yields to the poet's. The sthāyibhāva (love) transforms into the poet's delight at his own craft (camatkāra). The potsherd is both vessel and namesake. Flagged as application: Abhinava does not explicitly name this shift.

notes.craft_notes: Sthāyin: rati sharpened by viyoga — verse color is violence inside tenderness (bank rasa for this verse: śṛṅgāra turning to vīra). Sanskrit first: manmathe ca hṛdi hantum udyate / proṣitapramadayedam udyate — yamaka pair udyate×udyate closing both halves; two arisings, one event (argmap INF). Firing rows: row 9 (yamaka → anaphora rises…rises, inherited from frozen L3, kept whole — the pair IS the verse); row 8 (vowel music: with→beside at the close-swell — long vowel lets the line breathe where with-him dies short; bright kill against soft beside-him enacts rati softening vīra at the close); close-shape arrested not settled (the wound opens here; the song settles only at v9's question).
